messages:
maria_support: FYI ticket #7891 from acme-inc on dedicated cluster ded-chi-4. At ~12:03 UTC they saw sustained 429s for ~7m during a traffic spike. They say autoscaler did not add replicas fast enough — min_replicas=2, max_replicas=12, target_cpu=70. Traffic jumped ~50 -> ~400 rps. Attached logs below.

maria_support: logs snippet from control plane: 
```
[12:02:59] autoscaler: observed desired_replicas=8, current_replicas=2, scaling_disabled=false
[12:03:05] scheduler: pending pods 6, no nodes available in nodegroup-usw2-a (quota exhausted)
[12:03:05] autoscaler: decision=scale_up requested_nodes=4 reason=need_capacity but provisioner returned pending_provisioning=4 (pending)
[12:03:10] api: 429 Too Many Requests from frontend. queue_length=180
[12:09:15] autoscaler: node_provision_timeout for request id xyz timed out after 600s
```

maria_support: Repro steps customer provided: 1) send burst 400rps to dedicated route /v1/generate for model rdl-2 2) observe 429s within 30s 3) wait ~6-8m for manual scale to finish.

lucas_runtime: :eyes: can you paste the autoscaler config and the cluster's provisioner logs? Suspect two possibilities: (A) node quota exhausted in cloud so nodes stuck provisioning, or (B) autoscaler stabilization/cooldown prevented aggressive scaling. Also which node pool is used (spot vs on-demand)?

maria_support: autoscaler config snippet from console: 
```
minReplicas: 2
maxReplicas: 12
stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300
cooldownSeconds: 120
provisioner: gce-usw2-spot-pool
nodeProvisionTimeoutSeconds: 600
burstCapacity: 0
```

nina_infra: I looked at cloud console, us-west2-a has reached GPU quota for our project — 0 GPUs available. There are 4 instances in PROVISIONING state for the new nodegroup since 12:03. Cloud returned RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED which makes the cloud-provider keep the VM pending. That explains pending_provisioning=4.

nina_infra: temporary mitigation: (1) switch provisioner to fallback on-demand pool (gce-usw2-ond) or (2) manually bump quota for the project, or (3) increase burstCapacity to allow pre-warmed nodes.

oncall_ben: I manually scaled the replica count to 6 at 12:10 and customer error rate dropped to normal by 12:12. Manual scale log: scaled ded-chi-4 from 2->6, pods scheduled on existing spare nodes. Leaving note: we should not leave manual step as permanent fix. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: deploy service: autoscaler v2.1.4 rolled out to ded clusters at 2026-03-16T11:58:00Z (yesterday). No immediate errors in the rollout logs but it changed the default burstCapacity from 2->0.

lucas_runtime: that rollout change is suspicious. BurstCapacity=0 means no pre-provisioning buffer for short spikes. Combined with nodeProvisionTimeoutSeconds=600 and GPU quota exhaustion you get this stall. Suggest action items: (A) revert autoscaler burstCapacity default to 2 for ded clusters while we investigate, (B) reduce stabilizationWindowSeconds to 60 for high-throughput routes, (C) add a fallback policy to route low-latency requests to a warm small on-demand pool.

customer-success-amy: Customer impact summary: acme-inc experienced user-facing 429s for ~7m, affecting ~8% of traffic in their peak window. They've asked for timeline + credit. Please prioritize recovery path.

maria_support: Agreed. Immediate next steps I'm doing now: 1) create infra ticket to request temporary GPU quota bump for us-west2-a (nina assigned) 2) oncall to keep manual scale until quota resolves (ben) 3) runtime to revert burstCapacity change or patch autoscaler config (lucas) 4) CS to send customer incident summary + ETA (amy).

nina_infra: I opened cloud-ticket-1227 requesting quota emergency for GPUs and started a fallback provisioning to gce-usw2-ond. If quota is approved nodes should appear in ~4-6m.

lucas_runtime: I'll prepare a hotfix to set burstCapacity=2 and lower stabilizationWindowSeconds to 60 for the ded cluster autoscaler policy. Will test in staging then rollout.

oncall_ben: Leaving this thread open until we confirm quota increase and autoscaler patch. If anyone wants to take over pager, ping me. :hand: 

maria_support: Thanks all. I'll post final incident summary and the customer credit proposal once we have exact timings.

maria_support: TL;DR root cause: autoscaler rollout set burstCapacity=0 + cloud GPU quota exhaustion -> new nodes stuck provisioning -> scale-up stall -> 429s. Short-term fix: manual scale + emergency quota + revert burstCapacity. Long-term: add pre-warm policy and run autoscaler e2e on quota-constrained scenarios. :spiral_calendar:
